name: co-VC dimension of Half-intervals
details: Exact finite endpoint correction on the stated class domain. Original record preserved at sync/covc_endpoint_corrections/originals/023_covc_dimension_halfintervals.json.
proof: The class is $\{[i]:1\le i\le n\}$, so coordinate1 is constantly one; its missing zero trace gives a hollow one-star. For $n=1$ the domain has one coordinate. For $n=2$, the two full traces are $10,11$ and neither absent trace has both one-coordinate neighbours present, so coVC is one. For $n\ge3$, projection to coordinates2 and3 has traces $00,10,11$, whose absent $01$ is the centre of a hollow two-star. Every projection is a chain under inclusion, and a hollow star of size at least three has two incomparable realized neighbours (among three centre bits, two agree; flipping those two bits gives incomparable neighbours). Hence no larger hollow star occurs.
